messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sustained high queue depth on dedicated-pool-7 (us-west-2). avg queue_size=420, p95 latency > 1200ms, error_rate spike to 6%. Trigger: queue-depth > 300 for 3m.

maria: seeing it. oncall here. Is traffic coming from any single customer?

sam: checking flow logs and routing. preliminary shows a traffic surge from key-account: alpha-analytics, steady increase in long-chat streams. Could be a bad retry loop.

kevin: pinging dedicated infra. Pool 7 is at 100% of reserved instances; autoscaler didn't kick because burst toggles are off for this pool (by default).

maria: ops-bot, can you list affected routes and top origin IPs?

ops-bot: Top routes: /v1/generate (65%), /v1/stream (22%). Top customer tokens: alpha-analytics (55% of requests), beta-proxy (8%).

lydia: support here. I just opened a ticket for alpha-analytics and DM'd their account lead. They confirm they deployed a config change ~10m ago.

sam: customer impact: about 8% of requests are timing out or 5xx, most other requests are delayed. No billing anomalies yet. We should do live mitigations: qos, rate-limit, burst enable.

maria: agreed. Plan: 1) enable burst capacity on dedicated-pool-7 to absorb surge 2) add temporary traffic shaping via routing policy to limit alpha-analytics to 60% of pool 3) if still degraded, apply per-customer soft quota 4) keep canary fallback to CPU-backed model instances. Anyone object?

kevin: no objections. I can flip burst to "on" and bump max-instances to 12. Command coming.

kevin: ```
# enable burst
redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-pool-7 --burst-enabled true --burst-max-instances 12
# quick check
redwoodctl pools status --pool dedicated-pool-7
```

ops-bot: Action queued: burst enable requested by kevin. ETA to provision extra instances ~ 45s.

maria: while that provisions, applying a temporary routing policy to cap alpha-analytics traffic to 60% so the rest can be served. Sam, can you apply?

sam: applying routing policy now. ```
redwoodctl routing set-policy --pool dedicated-pool-7 --policy '{"alpha-analytics":0.6, "default":0.4}' --dry-run false
```

ops-bot: Routing policy applied. Requests redistributed.

incident-bot: pool update completed. 4 new instances provisioned, current instances=12. avg queue_size falling to 90. p95 latency 300ms.

maria: good. monitor for any oscillation. Lydia, can you update alpha-analytics contact that we've applied throttling and enabled burst?

lydia: messaged them: told them we enabled burst and applied a temporary cap. They say they'll roll back recent change if load doesn't normalize.

kevin: note: burst billing will incur overages vs reserved commit. I'll file a ticket to finance after incident.

sam: monitoring logs for retry loops — still seeing repeated client retries at 1.2s intervals. Might be aggressive client backoff config.

maria: let's also enable a short-lived soft quota for alpha-analytics to force exponential backoff on their side: reduce rate to 40 requests/sec for 10 minutes.

sam: applied soft quota. ```
redwoodctl quotas set --customer alpha-analytics --pool dedicated-pool-7 --rps 40 --duration 10m
```

ops-bot: Soft quota active. 429 responses will be returned when exceeded.

maria: status check in 2m. If things stay stable, we'll start rolling down burst and routing policy.

(2 minutes later)

ops-bot: metrics update: queue_size=35, p95 latency=180ms, error_rate=1.2%. Request distribution: alpha-analytics <= 60% as expected.

maria: looks stable. kevin, keep burst on but scale down max-instances to 10 to limit cost while we observe.

kevin: ```
redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-pool-7 --burst-max-instances 10
```

ops-bot: update accepted. New max-instances=10.

sam: recommend we document this mitigation sequence in the incident channel and schedule a post-incident runbook update: add a checklist for pools with burst off by default, include playbook to quickly enable burst + routing caps.

maria: agree. I'll do the handoff to night oncall in 20m. Current status: degraded -> partial mitigation. Actions taken: burst enabled, routing cap applied, soft quota added, customer notified. No data exfiltration, limited impact to latency and 5xxs under 2% now.

lydia: support notified customers A/B by email. alpha-analytics acknowledged.

kevin: I'll follow up to make sure autoscaler logs are captured for root cause. Might be misconfigured threshold preventing autoscale when queue grows slowly.

maria: handoff note for night oncall (@sam): keep burst enabled until 02:00 UTC or until metrics stable for 30m. If alpha-analytics doesn't rollback change, escalate to account manager and consider temporary hard quota.

sam: ack. I'll take second shift. Creating incident doc.```

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-335001 with severity=2. Postmortem assigned to kevin/sam.

maria: thanks team. closing thread here; leaving the oncall handoff note in #incidents. :white_check_mark:
